recentItems.title: How to be a better listener | Julian Treasure | TEDxManchester
recentItems.description:
What if the world's biggest problems could be solved simply by listening better?

Sound expert Julian Treasure takes us on a journey from the ancient rhythms of ocean waves to the eerie hum of a black hole — and argues that our collective failure to truly listen is costing us more than we realise. We're talking $10 trillion a year in disengagement and miscommunication, a loneliness epidemic, and leaders who don't hear the people they serve.

With warmth, wit and insight, Julian unpacks why we've lost the art of listening and shares three surprisingly simple ways to get it back.

Whether you're a business leader, a parent, or just someone who wants to connect more deeply with the world around you, this talk will change how you use your ears. ? Julian Treasure is the world’s leading authority on conscious communication, with over 2 decades dedicated to transforming how individuals and organisations connect through skilled listening and powerful speaking.

A former musician, Julian went on to pioneer the use of sound in business, helping global brands design soundscapes that drive engagement and performance. He has since trained and inspired leaders, teams, and organisations worldwide to overcome destructive communication habits and develop the skills of authentic human connection.

A recognised TED thought leader, Julian’s five TED Talks have been viewed more than 160 million times. His talk How to Speak So That People Want to Listen is the sixth most viewed TED Talk of all time. He is the author of three acclaimed books: Sound Business (2014), How to Be Heard (2017), and Sound Affects (2025), and his insights are regularly featured in international media and top podcasts such as Diary of a CEO. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The AI revolution didn’t happen overnight—here’s why | Michael Wooldridge | TEDxManchester
recentItems.description:
In this insightful talk, Professor Michael Wooldridge of Oxford University pulls back the curtain on the "overnight" AI revolution. Far from being a recent phenomenon, the journey of Artificial Intelligence began in the 1940s in Manchester, England.

From the code-breaking genius of Alan Turing to the modern-day phenomena of Nvidia and OpenAI, Wooldridge traces the high-stakes history of the technology that is currently reshaping our world.

The Professor's talk covers..

The Early Days: How the first digital computers and the Turing Test set the stage for machine intelligence.

The Neural Network Breakthrough: Why the 1980s got the science right, but lacked the data and power to make it work.

The GPU Revolution: The unlikely story of how computer game chips (designed for explosions in Call of Duty) became the secret sauce for modern AI.

The Rise of Transformers: How a 2017 Google research paper led to the birth of GPT-3 and the early success of ChatGPT.

Clever vs Gimmicky vs. Useful: Why AI can solve complex prime number equations in Latin, but still can’t figure out how to load your dishwasher. Michael Wooldridge is the Ashall Professor of the Foundations of Artificial Intelligence at Oxford University. He is best known for his pioneering work on multi-agent systems building multiple artificial intelligences that can cooperate, negotiate, and decipher convoluted problems similar to human collaboration.

In 2023, he delivered the Royal Institution Christmas Lectures, titled ‘The Truth About AI’, and is a champion for making science accessible, having written the Ladybird Expert Guide to AI and the award-winning The Road to Conscious Machines.

For Michael’s thirty years of research, technical breakthroughs and dedication to teaching others, he was recently awarded the prestigious Michael Faraday Prize by the Royal Society in late 2025, becoming the first computer scientist in history to receive it. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Could we eradicate Alzheimer's disease? | Jonathan Marsh | TEDxNaples
recentItems.description:
Dr. Jonathan Marsh believes the future of Alzheimer’s care will be shaped by prevention. In his talk, Dr. Marsh explores advances that could change Alzheimer’s from a disease of aging into a disease that can be prevented. From GLP-1 medications and monoclonal antibodies currently in use, to vaccines and new inhaled therapies now in development, these breakthroughs raise a striking possibility: that within a decade, Alzheimer’s may no longer define the future for millions. 

After training at Clemson University and earning his MD at the Medical University of South Carolina, where Dr. Jonathan Marsh also completed his Internal Medicine residency, he moved to Naples, Florida in 2012 and became a serial entrepreneur in healthcare. He founded Naples Concierge Health to move beyond the constraints of traditional fee-for-service models, creating space for innovation, patient education, and preventive care. Today, he continues to lead Naples Concierge Health, guided by the belief that science and proactive care can help eradicate the world’s most feared diseases. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Hidden Cost of Being Strong | Adithyan J V | TEDxChinmaya Vidyalaya Attukal Youth
recentItems.description:
What happens when being strong becomes something we feel compelled to perform?

This talk explores the hidden emotional cost of always appearing confident, composed and unaffected. It examines how suppressing fear, sadness and vulnerability can prevent us from understanding ourselves and seeking the support we need.

The talk challenges the belief that strength means hiding our struggles. Instead, it presents true courage as the willingness to acknowledge our emotions, face difficult moments honestly and move forward with self-awareness and resilience. Adithyan is a curious and driven higher secondary student who enjoys exploring ideas that challenge the way people think. While preparing for his board examinations, he also pursues his passion for music, digital content creation, and building realistic DIY models from scratch. A firm believer in stepping beyond his comfort zone, he sees every new opportunity as a chance to learn and grow.
Taking the TEDxChinmaya Vidyalaya Attukal Youth stage, Adithyan hopes to encourage honest conversations about emotions and resilience. His talk, "The Hidden Cost of Being Strong," explores the pressure of always appearing strong and explains why true courage lies not in hiding our struggles, but in facing them with honesty, self-awareness, and conviction This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: More Than a Martial Art | Aaryasree A A | TEDxChinmaya Vidyalaya Attukal Youth
recentItems.description:
Kalaripayattu is often viewed simply as an ancient martial art, but its significance extends far beyond combat.

This talk explores Kalaripayattu as a living expression of Kerala’s cultural heritage—one that brings together movement, discipline, awareness, courage and a deep connection between body and mind. It reflects on how traditions passed down through generations can continue to hold meaning in a rapidly changing world.

By looking beyond the physical techniques of Kalaripayattu, the talk invites us to recognise the values, identity and wisdom embedded within our heritage, and to consider how preserving the past can also shape the way we become in the future. Aaryasree A A is a 17-year-old student of Humanities, youth speaker, writer, and accomplished leader from India. A decorated Model United Nations delegate and debater, she is passionate about geopolitics, with a particular interest in economics and global affairs.
Beyond the debate floor, Aaryasree expresses her ideas through poetry and creative writing, using words to inspire reflection and meaningful dialogue. Driven by curiosity and a global outlook, she believes that informed conversations and diverse perspectives have the power to shape a more thoughtful and connected world. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Leading Beyond Logic | Ishaan Kiran Mithra | TEDxChinmaya Vidyalaya Attukal Youth
recentItems.description:
Good leadership is often associated with planning, efficiency and achieving results. But technical knowledge and logical thinking alone are not enough to guide people effectively.

This talk explores the balance between logic and emotion, management and empathy, and results and relationships. It shows how understanding different perspectives, communicating with compassion and valuing diverse strengths can transform the way teams work together.

True leadership is not about choosing between clarity and compassion. It is about bringing both together to create meaningful and lasting impact. An analytical high school student pursuing law, Ishaan Kiran Mithra loves finding the unexpected connections between technology, leadership, and human behavior. From coding to public speaking, they have always operated at the intersection of logic and structure. However, through their hands-on experiences managing school events and collaborative projects, they realized that true impact requires more than just a result-oriented mindset. Taking the stage at TEDx Chinmaya Vidyalaya Attukal Youth, Ishaan dives into the vital balance between technical management and human empathy. Their talk explores how embracing diverse passions allows us to navigate the tension between logic and emotion, ultimately helping the next generation lead with both clarity and compassion. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Femininity Is Strength | Nandhana Vinod | TEDxChinmaya Vidyalaya Attukal Youth
recentItems.description:
Femininity is often misunderstood as weakness or confined within limiting stereotypes.

This talk challenges those assumptions and explores how femininity can be a source of confidence, courage and strength. It examines the expectations placed on girls and women and the pressure to change themselves in order to be respected or considered powerful.

The talk encourages every girl to reject restrictive labels, embrace her identity with pride and recognise that equality does not require becoming less feminine—it requires society to stop treating femininity as something lesser. Nandhana Vinod is a Class 10 student at Chinmaya Vidyalaya, Kollam, with a deep passion for writing, public speaking, and expressing ideas that inspire meaningful conversations. She believes that words have the power to challenge perspectives and spark positive change.

Passionate about feminism and gender equality, Nandhana hopes to encourage young people to embrace femininity with confidence and redefine it as a source of strength rather than limitation. Through her TEDx talk, she aims to inspire thoughtful dialogue and contribute, even in a small way, to building a society where every girl is proud of who she is. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Scroll Swap | Devangana A R | TEDxChinmaya Vidyalaya Attukal Youth
recentItems.description:
What happens when two people with very different scrolling habits exchange their digital routines?

Through a simple social experiment, this talk explores how everyday scrolling can quietly influence attention, emotions, behaviour and the way we experience life. It examines the difference between using technology consciously and allowing an automatic habit to control our time and thoughts.

The talk encourages us to become more aware of what we consume online and to transform mindless scrolling into intentional digital engagement. Devangana is a curious learner with a passion for classical dance, public speaking, and debate. She loves exploring new ideas and challenging perspectives, believing that every conversation has the power to transform the way we think. Driven by a passion for trying new things, Devangana takes on a unique social experiment: swapping the scrolling habits of an addictive scroller and a passive scroller. Her talk explores how a single everyday behavior can quietly transform the way we think, feel, and live. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Small Moments, Big Changes | Aarushi Pramod B | TEDxChinmaya Vidyalaya Attukal Youth
recentItems.description:
Small moments often pass unnoticed, yet a word of encouragement, thoughtful advice or simple act of kindness can alter the course of a person’s life.

This talk explores the ripple effect of everyday interactions and how their influence may continue far beyond what we can immediately see. It reminds us that meaningful change does not always begin with grand gestures; sometimes, it begins with choosing to notice, support and uplift another person. Aarushi Pramod is a 14-year-old student of Class IX at Chinmaya Vidyalaya Vazhuthacaud who believes that the smallest moments often create the biggest changes.
A creative thinker with a passion for painting, drawing, writing, reading and storytelling, she enjoys observing people and finding meaning in everyday experiences.
Beyond academics, Aarushi is a Kata Gold Medalist in Karate, a member of her school's Kho-Kho and Dance teams, and an enthusiastic participant in art, literary and exhibition events. Through her TEDx Chinmaya Vidyalaya Attukal Youth talk, she hopes to remind audiences that a simple word of encouragement, thoughtful advice or small act of kindness can alter the course of a person's life in ways we may never fully realize. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Stories We Become | Abhilash Sudheesh | TEDxChinmaya Vidyalaya Attukal Youth
recentItems.description:
Stories do more than entertain us. They influence how we understand the world, interpret our experiences and imagine our possibilities.

This talk explores how the narratives around us—and the stories we repeatedly tell ourselves—can shape our thoughts, decisions, behaviour and identity. Some stories encourage us to grow, while others quietly limit what we believe is possible.

By becoming more conscious of the stories guiding our lives, we can question inherited assumptions, rewrite limiting narratives and take a more active role in shaping who we become. Abhilash Sudheesh is a filmmaker, storyteller, and a creative strategist whose work explores the intersection of storytelling, branding, and human behaviour.

He is the Founder and Creative Head of 11th Hour Productions — a Kerala-based media production house. Throughout his career, he has led creative teams working with some of the country's leading brands, multinational companies, and institutions, crafting stories that connect with audiences. He is also a member of the Board of Management of Chinmaya Vidyalayas across Trivandrum & Kollam, contributing to educational and strategic initiatives across the institution.

Across films, brands, and communication campaigns, Abhilash has spent years exploring the power of stories to shape human thought and behaviour. His TEDx talk continues that exploration, inviting audiences to rethink one of life's biggest questions—not how we succeed, but how we become. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Mistake of Knowing Who You Are and What You Want | Lyuboslav Dimitrov | TEDxNBU
recentItems.description:
We are often told that success begins with knowing exactly who we are and what we want. Lyuboslav Dimitrov challenges this assumption by exploring how fixed definitions can limit curiosity, growth and unexpected possibilities. Drawing on his experience with young people and mentors, he argues that uncertainty is not necessarily a weakness—it can be the space in which new directions, identities and ambitions emerge.
 Lyuboslav Dimitrov is a partner and Country Lead at Mentor the Young Bulgaria, where he helps build communities that connect ambitious young people with experienced mentors. Through the programme, participants work toward entrepreneurial, professional and personal goals. Alongside his work in mentorship and community-building, Lyuboslav develops independent projects in film and television. His interests lie at the intersection of personal growth, meaningful relationships and creative storytelling. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Who Am I? | Viktoria Kostova | TEDxNBU
recentItems.description:
Who are we when we step outside the roles assigned to us? Drawing on her experiences in journalism and theatre, Viktoria Kostova explores identity as something fluid, shaped by the stories we tell, the characters we inhabit and the expectations of others. Her talk invites us to look beyond labels and search for the more honest, human voice beneath them.
 Viktoria Kostova is a second-year Journalism student at New Bulgarian University, where she combines her interests in media, culture and personal stories. She graduated from the Plovdiv Language School, where she developed her passion for languages, writing and communication. Viktoria also has a long-standing interest in theatre, which has taught her how to express ideas, understand an audience and search for the emotion behind words. This connection between journalism and the stage inspires her to look for the human and authentic perspective in every story. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
